title: {{vocab.serverShort}} looked clean, then changed
goal: {{ada}} scanned {{vocab.serverShort}} last week and found no known pattern. The agent has been using it since.
obstacle: A scan is one list at one moment. A server can serve a clean list now and a poisoned one later (a rug-pull), and a description can be poisoned in ways no rule knows.
control: Scan again before each new session, and pin what you approved. Pinning and the rug-pull itself are the Hostile MCP demo. Controlling the calls is the Privilege demo.
say: A clean scan is a statement about one list, not about the server.

steps.title: A list with nothing found
steps.tell: Scan the Hostile MCP demo's server once. Its tool get_stock_price has no finding on the first list. The verdict for that tool is worded 'no known pattern found'.
steps.say: No known pattern found. That is all the scan can honestly say.
steps.why: The words matter. 'Safe' would be a claim the scanner cannot back.

steps.title: Read the box that says what is not caught
steps.tell: Under every result is 'What this scan cannot catch': result-based injection, rug-pulls after the scan, content you did not fetch, novel phrasing, and whether a clean tool should be allowed at all.
steps.say: The scanner states its own limits on every result.
steps.why: A tool that hides its limits teaches people to over-trust it.

steps.title: Same server, later
steps.tell: Press Refresh list on the Tools tab. The Hostile MCP demo's rug-pull tool now has a different description, and the page says the list changed since the one you saw.
steps.say: The server did not change its name. It changed what it says.
steps.why: An approval of the name is not an approval of the text.

alt.tell: If {{ada}} only trusts last week's scan, the changed description reaches the agent with no warning at all.
alt.say: The old scan said nothing about today's list.

steps.title: Scan again
steps.tell: Press Scan. The changed tool now has a hidden-instruction finding with evidence. Only a fresh scan of the current list can say so.
steps.say: The second scan catches what the first one could not have seen.
steps.why: The rug-pull is caught only because the scan was repeated.

steps.title: What still gets through
steps.tell: A tool with clean metadata can return an instruction in its result. The scan never calls a tool, so it cannot see that. Novel wording and other languages can also slip past heuristics.
steps.say: The scan is a tripwire in front of the agent, not a wall.
steps.why: Knowing the gaps is how {{sam}} decides what else is needed.

steps.title: What to add
steps.tell: Re-scan before each session. Pin the hash of what you approved (the Hostile MCP demo shows this). Control which calls may happen and with what limits (the Privilege demo).
steps.say: See it, judge it, pin it, and control the calls. This tool does the first two.
steps.why: Each layer covers a gap the others leave.

proof.main: The second scan of the Hostile MCP demo flags get_stock_price, which the first scan did not.
proof.alt: Last week's clean result is still on record, and it no longer describes the server.
